info.title: Enterprise GPT API
info.summary: Every endpoint the Enterprise GPT screens call.
info.description:
The API contract between the Enterprise GPT backend (Lane R, Lane K) and the interface.
Written in phase zero and wired in phase five, per `docs/plan/delivery-plan.md`. It is
published as a schema, not a document: `egpt_retail/api/models/_generated.py` is generated
from it, and the stub server in `egpt_retail/api/stub/` serves each operation's declared
examples so a screen can be pointed at the contract before any of it is implemented.

**Derived, not invented.** The endpoint inventory maps the prototype's local-storage seam
(`frontend/src/storage/*.js`) accessor by accessor, then corrects the four places where a
literal mapping would bake a demo artifact into the API (see CHANGELOG.md, 1.0.0).

**What this contract does not re-specify.** Chat, run streaming and session history are
already served by the framework and must not be duplicated here:

| Need | Framework endpoint |
|---|---|
| Chat with an agent, streamed | `POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs` (SSE) |
| Conversation history | `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{session_id}` |
| Scheduled runs (definition, pause, history) | `/schedules`, `/schedules/{schedule_id}` |
| Use case definitions as versioned components | `/components` |
| Health and configuration | `GET /health`, `GET /config` |

This document adds only what those lack: the retail resources, the delivery fields on a
schedule, and the provenance record every answer writes.

**Every list is unpaginated in 1.0.0.** Phase-zero data volumes do not need it and adding
it later is additive (a `next_cursor` field). Recorded in CHANGELOG.md as a known gap.

**Semantic layer.** The `semantic` paths are the HTTP surface of Lane K's
`SemanticRead` contract (`egpt_retail/contracts/semantic.py`, v1.0.0). The stub behind
them in phase zero is `StubSemanticRead`; K5 replaces it in phase two without changing
a caller.

servers.description: The phase-zero stub server (`api/stub/server.py`'s default port, chosen so it does not collide with R1).

viewer.description: Reads dashboards, results and the catalog.

analyst.description: Viewer, plus authors use cases and KPIs and runs the playground.

admin.description: Analyst, plus activates use cases at level three and above and manages sources.

bearerAuth.description:
A JWT issued by the identity provider (Entra ID in the target deployment; an offline
RS256 key pair against a mounted JWKS file in local verification). The `scope` claim
carries the space-separated scope strings; `x-egpt-scopes` on each operation names
what it requires.

AlertDefinition.description:
A rule over a `scalar` KPI (R12): KPI, operator, threshold, scope, severity, recipient.
Evaluated by a deterministic executor after every gold materialisation. A `rowset` KPI
cannot be alerted on and is refused with 422.

window.description: How long the condition must hold before firing. Null fires on the first breach.

recommended_actions.description: Authored with the rule, rendered on every event it fires. Not generated.

use_case_id.description: The use case a fired event links to, if any.

AlertEvent.description: One firing of a definition. What the inbox, the bell and the monitor page show. Mutating it never touches the definition.

rule.description: The definition rendered as a sentence, frozen at firing time.

run_id.description: The evaluation run that fired it.

AlertEventKpi.description: The KPI reading that fired the event, frozen at firing time.

AlertScope.description: Which rows of a non-overall KPI the rule applies to.

grain_column.description:
Which gold-view column `grain_value` is matched against, when the KPI's rows carry
more than one dimension column (e.g. both `region` and `channel`) and a bare
`grain_value` could equal more than one of them. Optional and additive (CHANGELOG
1.1.2): a legacy definition with no `grain_column` is matched only when the result
set is unambiguous on shape alone -- refused, not guessed, when it is not.

AnalyticsFeasibility.description: `ready` when gold holds a row; `buildable` when the first run computes it.

score.description: The lexical match, for ordering; not a probability.

why.description: The ask's own words that chose this KPI.

question.description: The ask, in the person's own words.

recipient.description: A default address when the ask names none.

kind.description: A standing report; a question about one movement run once and promoted if kept; or the at-risk kind (1.13.0, K26) that scores every open subject and ends in a recommendation or an alert.

dimensions.description: The grains the chosen KPIs break down by.

comparison.description: Set only when the ask compares (a period named, a change asked about); null means the numbers are reported as they are.

window.description: Days the numbers cover, when the ask names a period (last week, monthly); null means each KPI's own declared window.

uncovered.description: Words of the ask no registered KPI covers.

AnswerBlock.description: One renderable block of an answer -- a finding, a table, a chart, a recommendation. The playground's answer format owns the inner shape; the report only needs the id and kind to pin it.

Autonomy.description: `copilot` surfaces decision cards for a person; `autopilot` executes within guardrails.

BulkProposalDecisionRequest.description: A single source harvest produces hundreds of proposals; nobody clicks through them one gate at a time (G5).

BusinessArea.description:
One node of the business hierarchy. `id` is a term from the deployment's `business_area`
vocabulary (shipped ontology plus overlay, D9/G10). `supported` is derived from confirmed
mappings (K9), never asserted; `concept_count`, `table_count` and `reason` are the
evidence behind it, so a screen can show why as well as whether.

concept_count.description: Accepted concepts in this area that have a confirmed table mapping (K9). 0 when unsupported.

reason.description: K9's one-sentence account of why the area is or is not supported, ready to render.

BusinessAreaHierarchyWrite.description: An overlay may add areas and annotate them. It may not remove or redefine a core area (G10); a request that tries is refused with 409.

BusinessAreaId.description:
A business area identifier. In 1.0.0 this is the shipped `business_area` vocabulary
(`egpt_retail/ontology/vocabularies.json`) plus whatever a customer overlay adds, so it is
a string validated at runtime against the deployment's vocabulary, not an enum.

BusinessAreaList.description: Areas this deployment supports, derived from confirmed mappings (K9). Empty means no source has been connected, never that the ontology is empty.

CaseExpected.description:
What a golden case expects (1.6.0) -- the outcome (`created`, or an exception class) and
header values, authored by accepting a run's output or supplied on upload.

sample_id.description: Set on the curated purchase-order set only.

ChartAxis.description: One result column a `query` tile plots. `kind` matters on the x axis only.

ChatFilters.description: The date window every answer in the playground is scoped to. Bound as the as-of window on every read, so the intro copy and the data agree.

parent_field.description: The child's reference to the parent, filled with the parent's new id.

CloudProfile.description: Where this deployment runs. Read-mostly; under D3 it is one customer's tenancy and the value is set at deploy time.

is_personal_data.description: Set by enrichment and confirmed by a person. Drives the compliance tags a provenance record carries.

sampled_values.description: Values the harvest actually saw. Bounded; never the whole column.

concept.description: The concept this column is a property of, once review confirmed it.

meaning.description: What this column identifies, as accepted through review. Distinct from `description`, which is what the schema author wrote.

ColumnUsage.description: One column the formula reads, and why -- "the columns it uses". Column-names the agent declares, not a parse of `sql` -- it already reads every table's columns to write the formula, so this is it stating what it used, the same trust `derived_from_tables` already carries for tables.

why.description: One line: why this column and not a sibling that could plausibly mean the same thing, e.g. "Two time columns; the month cannot cut a 28-day window."

definition.description: The column's own definition from the semantic layer (`Column.meaning`, the reviewed definition -- falling back to `Column.description`, the schema's raw comment, when enrichment hasn't reached the column yet) -- what it holds, not why this KPI reads it (that's `why`). Read-only enrichment, like `SourceTableStatus.description`; not part of what a create/update or the agent's own output carries -- always `""` on write, on a suggestion preview, or when the semantic layer has none.

ColumnUsageRole.description: What one column contributes to the formula -- the "USED AS" badge on "the columns it uses".

Concept.description: What a concept means, and how to turn it into rows. Every field arrived through a proposal a person accepted.

sql_filter.description: The SQL boolean fragment that scopes this concept. Interpolated as a PREDICATE parameter in a KPI formula. Never built from user input.

metrics.description: KPI identifiers reachable from this concept.

Confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports a proposal or suggestion. Not a probability; a reviewer reads it to decide what to look at first.

ContentOrigin.description: Whether a document shipped with the product or is the customer's own (G17).

DashboardChartSuggestion.description:
One composed chart. `source: kpi` reuses a registered, ready KPI's own SQL through gold
(`kpi_identifier` set, `query` null); `source: query` carries SQL the agent composed from
the tables it was shown (`query` set). Every `query` chart passed through the warehouse
read guard and a bounded dry run before reaching the caller; `guard` and `preview` say what
happened. `description` is written for the person reading the dashboard and is theirs to
edit.

DashboardFilterColumn.description:
A column exposed as an end-user filter on the published dashboard -- a definition, never a
selection: it names which `(table, column)` becomes a dropdown, not a value someone picked
in it. What a viewer picks is per-viewer, transient view-time state carried in the URL of
`GET /dashboards/{id}/data`, never part of the saved dashboard (R13.1).

DashboardFilterValues.description: Distinct values of one of a dashboard's chosen filter columns, for its dropdown.

DashboardSuggestion.description:
A suggested dashboard for the given purpose, editable before creation: a name and the
charts the agent composed from the selected metrics and the tables behind them. `filters`
is always empty here -- a filter is now a chosen `(table, column)` (R13.1), which the agent
has no basis to pick on its own; a person adds filter columns afterward in the dashboard
builder. `context` says what the agent was shown.

notes.description: Empty on a clean run; otherwise what was missing, why the list is short, or what was dropped.

DashboardSuggestionRun.description:
One run of the dashboard suggestion agent, started by `POST /dashboards/suggestions` and
polled at `GET /dashboards/suggestions/{run_id}` -- the same run-then-poll shape #254 gave
KPI suggestions, for the same reason: a live model call takes long enough that it does not
belong inside one request, and the api serves from more than one instance. `result` is
present once `status` is `succeeded`; `error` is why there is none, present once `failed`.
A run whose executor was lost (the serving instance restarted mid-run) is reported `failed`
by the read side after the deployment's timeout plus a grace period, never `running` forever.

error.description: Written for the person polling. A timeout names the bound it hit.

DashboardSuggestionRunRequest.description:
What to run. `purpose` is the caller's own words for what the dashboard should help them
track. `kpi_identifiers` are the metrics the agent reads as context -- their definitions
and the tables behind them -- not a list it must tile one for one. `table_names` widens
the tables it may read beyond those the metrics name. `chart_budget` is a soft cap on
how many charts to compose; the agent may return fewer.

DashboardSuggestionRunStatus.description: Where a dashboard suggestion run is. The same four words as `KpiSuggestionRunStatus`.

DashboardSuggestionStage.description: Where a running suggestion is, for the person waiting. `reading` the metrics and tables, `drafting` charts, `guarding` each query, `previewing` each with real rows.

DeliveryChannel.description: Results are delivered in-app with an email pointer (D13). `email` and `slack` are pointers to the in-app result, never the result itself, so provenance stays attached.

support_floors.description: Rows a slice needs to be named, per sensitivity (clear, usual, more).

window.description: Days between the two periods; null means the KPI's own window.

as_of.description: The run date to size the periods at; null means today.

DraftStep3.description: Data scope. Every id here is a configured source, a knowledge collection or a semantic table -- validated on save, so the plan cannot reference something that does not exist.

Error.description:
The error body every non-2xx response carries. `detail` is written for the person who
sees it, never a stack trace. `code` is a stable machine token so a screen can branch on
it without parsing prose.

ExternalIntegration.description: A connector source (Lane C). Its data lands in object storage against the landing contract; this record is how the interface shows it.

ExternalIntegrationPatch.description: A partial update. Every field optional; omitted fields are unchanged. Same shape as `ExternalIntegrationWrite`.

ExtractionTemplate.description:
A document kind the Extract stage fills (1.4.0). The three shipped ones are rows of the
same shape; a template a person assembles on the form, or the model drafts from a
description and an example, is stored on the use case's spec as the `extraction template`
parameter and runs the same extractor. Nothing about a template is code.

id.description: Slug; derived from the label when absent.

record.description: What one document becomes: order, payable, return, receipt.

source.description: Where the template came from; `authored` when absent.

notes.description: What the model was unsure about; empty on a clean draft.

description.description: The use case's own words: what arrives and what it should become.

label.description: The document kind's name, when the person has one.

example_text.description: The text of an example document, when one is at hand.

example_document_b64.description: A PDF of an example document, base64; its text layer is read server-side.

name.description: snake_case field name; the extraction step fills exactly this.

hint.description: Where on the document the field is usually found, for the extractor.

rationale.description: One sentence a customer can act on, naming the missing tables.

FeasibilityVerdict.description: The result of a set difference, never an opinion. Mirrors `egpt_retail.contracts.kpi.FeasibilityVerdict`.

FormulaExplanation.description: A human-readable rendering of `sql`, for the discovery panel's FORMULA card -- not a numerator/denominator KPI-to-KPI link (there is no such linkage), just two plain-English labels a renderer can lay out as a fraction. Optional; a KPI without one falls back to showing only the raw SQL.

expression_before.description: Everything in the expression before the ratio, or the whole expression verbatim when there is no ratio -- e.g. "value = ROUND( 100 x" or "value = COUNT(*)".

numerator_label.description: Plain-English description of the ratio's numerator, e.g. "count of buy inquiries with converted_to_quote = true". Null when the formula has no ratio.

denominator_label.description: Plain-English description of the ratio's denominator. Null in exactly the same cases as `numerator_label`.

expression_after.description: Everything after the ratio, or empty when there is no ratio -- e.g. ", 1 )".

condition_label.description: A plain-English "where ..." sentence describing the formula's filter/window. Null when there's nothing beyond the ratio itself worth naming.

FreshnessStamp.description: The stamp every gold row carries, surfaced. Without it a stale answer is indistinguishable from a wrong one.

detail.description: What to connect or confirm to close the gap. Written for the customer.

GapCheck.description: A deterministic check of the spec against the semantic layer and the KPI registry. Set differences and join-path lookups; no model is consulted.

GapKind.description:
`missing_parameter` (1.1.0, R9): a slot the chosen autonomy shape requires (build plan, section 07)
that the draft and spec do not fill -- metrics, dimensions, comparison, schedule, recipient for
Inform; candidates, guardrails, approver, write target and more for Recommend and Act. `subject`
is the parameter name; `detail` says which builder field fills it, or that none exists yet.

`unknown_grain` (1.1.1, R9): `spec.grain` is not in this deployment's grain vocabulary.
The same ground truth `spec_extractor.validate_spec` checks at extraction time, re-checked
here so a coined value is caught deterministically whether or not that validator ran first.
`subject` is the coined value; `detail` says to add it to the customer overlay or pick a
listed one.

last_result.description: The last verdict: outcome, expected outcome, each check, and what the run observed.

GoldenCaseUpdate.description:
Fields a person may change on a case (1.6.0). Absent fields are left alone; an explicit
null `expected` clears the expectation.

sender.description: The address the document is treated as sent from; the customer lookup reads its domain.

Grain.description: A term from the deployment's `grain` vocabulary (shipped ontology plus overlay). A string validated at runtime, not an enum -- see CHANGELOG 2.0.0 of the KPI formula shape.

GuardDecision.description: What R6's SQL guard decided. A refused statement never reached the database.

GuardrailRule.description:
One business guardrail (1.4.0): a kind applied to a field, with its parameters and the
exception it raises. The `guardrails` parameter of a `document_to_record` spec is a list
of these; the six purchase-order rows keep their ids and exception classes as a preset.

line_field.description: For total checks, the line field summed; for item checks, the resolved entity on the line.

GuardrailRuleKind.description: A kind of check the platform can evaluate (1.4.0). A guardrail is one of these applied to a field with parameters.

check.description: The check in plain words, with {field} and parameter placeholders.

needs.description: The master-data role the check reads, or null.

Harvest.description: One run of the deterministic metadata harvest (K4). No model is involved.

source_id.description: The configured internal source that was harvested.

snapshot_version.description: The semantic snapshot this harvest produced, once it succeeded.

proposals_created.description: How many enrichment proposals the run queued for review.

InternalSource.description: A warehouse or system-of-record connection. Under D4 connectors land raw files in storage and the warehouse is loaded from there, so most deployments have exactly one `postgres` source pointed at the warehouse.

InternalSourcePatch.description: A partial update. Every field optional; omitted fields are unchanged. Same shape as `InternalSourceWrite`.

on.description: The join predicate, exactly as it would appear after `ON`.

intermediate_tables.description: Tables traversed that are neither endpoint. A preflight check needs these.

JoinPathResponse.description:
Three outcomes, never a guess. `path` present: the tables connect. `path` null with HTTP
200: the graph holds no path, which is an answer and the one a preflight check acts on.
HTTP 503: the reader could not answer, which is not an answer. **Not 404 for "no path"**
-- every HTTP client collapses 404 into "empty", which is exactly the collapse the
contract exists to prevent.

Kpi.description:
One KPI, as the registry holds it (K11) and the discovery screen renders it. The formula
fields are the contract shape; the presentation fields are what the registry screen shows.
`feasibility` is embedded so the list renders its ready/partial/blocked badges without a
call per row -- it is still a set difference, computed on read, never stored.

identifier.description: `<concept>__<name>`, stable across edits. What provenance and gold rows reference.

sql.description: The formula with `{named}` placeholders. Returned only to callers holding `kpis:write`; a viewer sees the field absent.

formula_explanation.description: A human-readable rendering of `sql`, for the FORMULA card. Gated behind `kpis:write` the same way `sql` is (`_may_read_sql`) -- its labels can name the same columns/tables the formula reads, so it is exactly the schema detail that gate exists to withhold from a `kpis:read`-only caller. Null for a hand-authored KPI, one adopted before this field existed, or a viewer without the scope.

column_usage.description: The formula's own account of which columns it reads and why -- "the columns it uses". Gated behind `kpis:write` the same way `sql` is; always `[]` for a `kpis:read`-only caller, a hand-authored KPI, or one adopted before this field existed. This KPI's own `table_usage` (fact/lookup role, join notes) is not a separate list here -- it rides along on each of `source_table_status`'s entries instead, since both describe the same tables.

rationale.description: Why the model proposed this KPI -- the sentence naming the tables or concepts it derives from, carried over from `KpiSuggestion.rationale` when the KPI was adopted. Null on a KPI authored by hand or adopted before this field existed.

business_value.description: What tracking this KPI lets someone decide or catch, carried over from `KpiSuggestion.business_value` on adopt. Null on a KPI authored by hand or adopted before this field existed.

dashboard_names.description: Names of the dashboards with a tile naming this KPI, sorted. Computed on read from the dashboard table, never stored on the KPI itself -- the same reference check `DELETE /kpis/{kpi_id}` already runs to refuse deleting a KPI still in use, generalized into a read path. Empty when nothing references it yet.

source_table_status.description: Each of `source_tables`' most recent load, from the warehouse's own load history -- only populated by `GET /kpis/{kpi_id}` (a list read never pays for N per-row warehouse queries), and only for a table that resolves to a known landed stream and has actually loaded at least once. Always `[]`, never a partial failure, when the warehouse is unreachable -- this is enrichment for the detail panel, not core KPI data.

KpiComputeResult.description:
The outcome of materialising one KPI for today's business date on demand -- the same
guarded pass the nightly run performs (`materialise_gold`), narrowed to one identifier.
`materialised` wrote today's row(s) and `GET /kpis/{kpi_id}/series` now has today's point;
`failed` names the formula's own error; `skipped` names why the pass would not run it.

KpiComputeStatus.description: Mirrors `gold.kpi_run.status` for the one KPI the call materialised.

KpiHealth.description: Freshness from gold (R5). Every gold row is stamped with source and computation time; this is that stamp surfaced.

as_of.description: The bound as-of date the last materialisation computed against.

KpiImportRequest.description: The CSV import panel. One row per KPI; columns match `KpiWrite` field names. Rows that fail construction are reported, not silently dropped.

KpiOrigin.description: Whether the KPI shipped with the product or the customer authored it.

KpiSeries.description:
One KPI's value over its last business dates, read from `gold.kpi_value` -- the same rows
a dashboard's `line`/`bar` tile plots, addressed by KPI rather than by tile. One point per
business date the KPI materialised for; a night with no row is absent, not `null` (`null`
means the formula returned NULL that night). Nothing is recomputed on read.

A KPI whose grain is not `overall` has one row per dimension value each night; `dimension`
names the one the points follow (the caller's choice, else the first seen) and
`dimensions` lists every value the latest night carried, so a screen can offer the others.

days.description: The window the points were read over, ending at `as_of`.

dimension.description: The grain-key values the points follow; `null` for an `overall` KPI.

dimensions.description: Every dimension the latest business date carried, in gold's row order, capped at 25.

value.description: The latest point's value; what a `number` tile of this KPI shows.

delta.description: `value` minus the previous point's value; `null` with fewer than two points.

KpiSeriesInterval.description: The spacing of `KpiSeries.points`. Gold materialises once a night (D7), so `day` is the only interval today; a coarser one would be an aggregation this contract does not define.

KpiSource.description: A user-added dataset in the KPI gallery (kpi-sources.js). More than a connection -- it carries the business context that turns rows into metrics.

source_id.description: The configured internal source it comes from, if known.

KpiSuggestion.description: A candidate KPI proposed by the K12 agent. Typed for direct rendering; every closed-set value from the deployment's vocabulary; traceable to named tables or it was invented.

rationale.description: One sentence naming the tables or concepts it derives from.

business_value.description: One or two sentences on why this metric is worth tracking -- what it lets someone decide or catch, distinct from `rationale`'s data provenance. Null on a suggestion from before this field existed.

formula_explanation.description: A human-readable rendering of `proposed_sql`, for the discovery card's preview before the KPI is adopted. Gated behind `kpis:write` the same way `proposed_sql` is -- its labels can name the same columns/tables the formula reads.

column_usage.description: Which columns `proposed_sql` reads and why -- "the columns it uses" on the discovery card's preview. Gated behind `kpis:write` the same way `proposed_sql` is.

table_usage.description: How `proposed_sql` uses each of `derived_from_tables` -- fact table or lookup, and what a lookup's join confirms. Gated behind `kpis:write` the same way `proposed_sql` is.

notes.description: Empty on a clean run; otherwise what was missing (the skill template's refusal shape).

KpiSuggestionRun.description:
One run of the K12 suggestion agent, started by `POST /kpis/suggestions` and polled at
`GET /kpis/suggestions/{run_id}` (#254). A run is two frontier-tier model calls and can
take minutes, so it is not served inside a request. `result` is the same
`KpiSuggestionList` the synchronous route returns, present once `status` is `succeeded`;
`error` is why there is none, present once `failed`. A run whose executor was lost
(the serving instance restarted mid-run) is reported `failed` by the read side after the
deployment's timeout plus a grace period, never `running` forever.

Two fields are for the person waiting: `phase` is the stage a `running` run is in, and
`typical_duration_seconds` is how long this deployment's recent runs took, so a screen
can set an expectation up front and show progress against it.

business_area.description: The area the run was narrowed to, or null for every area.

business_areas.description: The focus the run was started with (`KpiSuggestionRunRequest.business_areas`), echoed so a poller can see what was asked for. Empty when none.

ask.description: The request the run was started with (`KpiSuggestionRunRequest.ask`), echoed so a screen restoring a run can say what it was for. Null when none.

error.description: Written for the person polling. A timeout names the bound it hit.

phase.description:
Set while `running`, as each stage begins; null on a `queued` run and on a
`running` one that has not reached its first stage yet. Kept as it was once the run
is terminal, so a `failed` run says where it failed.

typical_duration_seconds.description:
The median wall-clock seconds of this deployment's last few successful runs, or null
before any has succeeded. An expectation, not a bound: a run may take longer, and the
deployment's timeout is the only limit.

KpiSuggestionRunPhase.description:
The stage a `running` suggestion run is in, in order: `reading` (the semantic layer the
agents are shown is being gathered), `proposing` (the model calls), `checking` (assembly
and feasibility against the snapshot). What a screen's stepper shows.

KpiSuggestionRunRequest.description:
What to run. Empty means suggest across every business area with no focus.
`business_areas` is the focus: the areas the customer cares about, handed to the agents
as a priority ("propose for these first"), never as a filter -- a proposal outside them
is kept when the data clearly supports it. `business_area` (one id) is the older
narrowing filter, applied to what comes back; kept for callers written against 1.1.5,
new callers should send `business_areas`.

business_areas.description: The focus. Each id must be in the deployment's vocabulary (422 otherwise); duplicates are dropped, order is kept.

ask.description:
What the customer wants to measure, in their own words ("Add KPI" -> AI generated).
Handed to the agents as the request to answer first, after the focus and before the
standing ask -- a steer, never a filter: what comes back is still every metric the data
supports, judged and stamped exactly as an unprompted run's would be, so a request the
harvest cannot back produces no invented metric, only the agent's note saying so.
Whitespace-only reads as absent.

KpiSuggestionRunStatus.description: Where a suggestion run is. The same four words as `HarvestStatus`, for the same shape.

KpiWrite.description: Authoring a KPI. The formula is validated at construction (declared parameters match placeholders, source tables cover the formula) and refused with 422 naming the defect.

formula_explanation.description: The suggestion's `formula_explanation`, resent verbatim when adopting a proposal so the registry keeps it. Optional; an update that omits it carries the stored value forward like every other optional field here.

column_usage.description: The suggestion's `column_usage`, resent verbatim when adopting a proposal. Optional; an update that omits it carries the stored value forward like every other optional field here.

table_usage.description: The suggestion's `table_usage`, resent verbatim when adopting a proposal. Optional; an update that omits it carries the stored value forward like every other optional field here.

rationale.description: The suggestion's `rationale`, resent verbatim when adopting a proposal so the registry keeps it. Optional; an update that omits it carries the stored value forward like every other optional field here.

business_value.description: The suggestion's `business_value`, resent verbatim on adopt. Optional, carried forward on update when omitted.

MailboxMessage.description:
One message in the connected mailbox that matches the use case's filter (1.6.0), without
its body or attachment bytes.

size.description: Bytes; a listing reads headers only, so attachments are not itemised.

processed_before.description: A live run already carried this message.

MappingFieldRow.description:
One target field and where its value comes from (1.5.0). `source` is a list of source
expressions over the resolved document, the first non-empty winning: a header field by
name (`po_number`), `line.<field>`, `customer.<key>`, `ship_to.<key>`, `product.<key>`,
`$pricebook_id`, `$today`, or a literal `=Draft`. `transform` is one of `date`,
`date_not_before_today`, `number`, `text:<n>`.

parent.description: The parent object's name, described live.

child.description: The per-line object's name, when there is one.

ModelTier.description: Which R8 routing tier this deployment binds the model to. Two deployments, composed through the escalation provider (G6).

description.description: The use case's own words, for the object labels to be read against.

child.description: The per-line object, when the template has lines and the target has one.

shipped_mapping.description: A shipped mapping's id for exactly this pair, when one exists.

Operator.description: `delta_*` compares the change against the previous period at the same grain.

ParameterKind.description: `predicate` is an interpolated SQL fragment from an accepted proposal; `scalar` is a driver-bound value. Never interchangeable.

PermissionLevel.description: The database role the source is connected with. `read_only` is the floor R6's guard sits on; a `read_write` source is never exposed to a model.

Plan.description: A view over the compiled workflow, never authored separately. Steps four and five of the prototype's wizard render this.

PlanStep.description: One step of the compiled workflow. `ref` is an executor name from the registry or a skill identifier -- the same strings the stored workflow holds.

permits_or_blocks.description: True for the executors that can stop the run -- preflight, guard, feasibility. Always false for an agent step, by the alignment rules.

advisory.description: Reported, never a gate: a failing advisory check (the golden cases) does not set allowed false or appear in blocked_by.

PreflightResult.description: Whether the use case may run now. A deterministic executor's answer; if it blocks, the reason is one a person can act on.

blocked_by.description: Names of the checks that failed.

ProbeResult.description:
One live connectivity probe (1.6.0): the platform actually opened the thing -- logged into
the mailbox, took a token from the target, read the master data, sent one call to the
model, read the golden cases -- and says what it found. Extra fields carry the numbers
(matching messages, row counts, pass counts).

Process.description: A named operational process within a business area. Read-only in 1.0.0 (see CHANGELOG).

Proposal.description:
One thing an agent proposed, and the record of what happened to it (K7,
`semantic.proposals.Proposal`). `target` is a plain string -- a concept name, a qualified
table, or (for `kind: kpi`) a metric identifier -- and `payload` carries whatever that
kind needs to be applied, which is why its shape is not fixed here: a `kpi` payload is a
whole KPI definition (`identifier`, `name`, `sql`, `grain`, `business_area`,
`source_tables`, plus display-only fields a reviewer wants -- `rationale`, `feasibility`,
`feasibility_reason`, `missing_tables`); a `use_case` payload is a question and the KPIs
it depends on. Nothing here reaches the graph, or the KPI registry, until `state` is
`accepted` (D10, G5) -- and even then, `applied_at` is what says whether it actually
landed, not `state` alone.

proposer.description: Which agent or person produced it. Never blank.

applied_at.description:
Set only once an accepted proposal's effect actually landed (a KPI saved to the
registry). An `accepted` proposal with `applied_at: null` is accepted-but-not-yet-
landed, or a kind with no consumer today (`use_case`) -- never assume `accepted`
alone means "done".

ProposalCounts.description: Totals by state, so the review screen can show its badge without a second call.

ProposalDecision.description: K7's `ReviewState`. One way out of `pending`, and no way back.

note.description: Optional reviewer note, kept with the decision.

ProposalKind.description:
What a proposal is about (K7's closed set, `semantic.proposals.ProposalKind`). `kpi` and
`use_case` are what `egpt-retail suggest` files; the other five are K4/K8 harvest-time
enrichment kinds this review screen also lists but does not specially render.

refused.description: Ids from the request that were not pending and so did not move. Empty on a plain list read.

ProposalRefusal.description:
One id in a decision request that did not move, and why. A bulk decision is not
atomic (K7's own `ReviewOutcome`, deliberately: eleven good decisions committing must
not be held hostage by a twelfth id a colleague decided a moment earlier) -- this is
how the caller finds out which one, and what its actual state is.

ProposalStatus.description:
Whether a row has been through review. Only `accepted` rows reach the graph (D10, G5).
A `proposed` row is returned only to a caller that passed `include_proposed=true`, and it
arrives labelled, so there is no way to receive an unreviewed synonym and mistake it for
a confirmed one.

Provenance.description:
The record every answer writes (alignment rule: "every answer writes a provenance
record"). Its shape is fixed here in phase zero so that R7 implements it rather than
designs it, and so the citation panel in the playground renders one thing. Holds what was
read, what was executed, what was sampled, how fresh each input was, what retrieval
returned, and which model tier answered.

semantic_snapshot.description: The semantic snapshot version every read in this run was answered from.

vocabulary_version.description: The shipped vocabulary version closed-set values were validated against.

ProvenanceModelTier.description: `none` when the run had no model step at all.

QueryGuardStatus.description:
What the warehouse read guard made of a query. `ok`: passed unchanged. `rewritten`: passed
after a mechanical fix -- a personal-data column dropped from the projection, a missing
LIMIT added, a LIMIT above the row cap lowered; `detail` says which. `refused`: not
runnable, `detail` says why; the chart is kept as a stub so the SQL can be fixed.

tables.description: The tables the statement reads, once parsed.

QueryPreview.description: One query's guard verdict and, when it ran, a bounded sample of its result.

sql.description: The statement as it would run -- the caller's, or the guard's rewrite of it.

error.description: The database's own refusal when the guard passed the statement but the warehouse did not (a typo in a column name, say).

table_names.description: Narrows the allow-list to these tables when given; otherwise the whole semantic layer.

address.description: An email address or a Slack channel. Empty for `in_app`.

Recommendation.description:
What an analytics use case hands to Decision Intelligence (1.13.0, K26): one subject (an
open quote and its account), its risk and the drivers behind it, and -- on a
recommendation -- the sales play the catalogue chose. An alert is the same record with
no action. Decision Intelligence, or a person on the screen, writes `status`; the use
case writes `outcome` when the horizon ends.

owner.description: Who acts: the rep on the quote.

risk_score.description: The probability the subject does not convert within the horizon.

horizon_days.description: The category's usual time to close.

action.description: The play; null on an alert.

context.description: The subject's row as scored (category, territory, stage, age against the usual, the account's RFM state, the last loss).

outcome.description: Written at the horizon's end: converted, lapsed, still_open, quoted_again, quiet.

expires_at.description: When the horizon ends and the outcome is looked up.

RecommendationDriver.description: One reason behind a risk score, grounded in the row's own value against the typical.

value.description: The row's own value: a number, or the category level.

typical.description: What the scored population averages; null for a category.

contribution.description: The feature's push on the log-odds of converting; negative is towards risk.

text.description: The driver in words, for the report and the alert.

counts.description: Records per status across the filter's use case (or all), for the screen's chips.

by.description: Who decided; the screen's user or the consuming use case.

RecommendedAction.description: The sales play the catalogue chose, who owns it, by when, and why it was chosen.

action.description: What to do, in the organisation's words.

owner.description: The role that owns the play.

because.description: The rule that chose it, in words.

RecordMapping.description:
How a resolved document becomes the target's objects (1.5.0): a parent object with its
field rows, an optional child repeated per line, the status field `created as` sets, and
the rollback action. The two Salesforce mappings that ship are rows of this shape; a
mapping the form assembles over the target's live object metadata is stored on the spec
as the `target objects` parameter and runs the same interpreter.

record.description: What the mapping creates, matched against a template's `record` when suggesting.

status_values.description: `created as` value -> the status written: {draft: Draft, active: Activated}.

RefreshSchedule.description:
How often the dashboard's numbers are recomputed -- the declared cadence, stored for the
scheduler to honour. `nightly` (the default) follows gold: as soon as the nightly
materialisation completes (D7). `daily` is once a day at a fixed morning time (06:00),
reading what gold holds. `weekly` is Monday mornings. `hourly` is every hour, capped in
practice by how often gold materialises. `manual` is only when asked. Distinct from
delivery (who is sent what, and when), which this contract does not yet carry.

RehearsalSource.description:
What a rehearsal runs over (1.6.0): chosen messages from the connected mailbox (writes
held, nothing flagged); the use case's own golden cases; or the set the platform
generates from the template. Absent means the mailbox when one is connected and a model
can read it, else the generated set.

run_id.description: The run the block came from, so its provenance is one hop away.

ResultShape.description: Mirrors `egpt_retail.contracts.kpi.ResultShape`. A `rowset` cannot be alerted on or trended.

RetrievalSource.description: The four legs the unified retrieval fans out across (K10).

RunMode.description:
`live` writes to the target and sends what it sends. `rehearse` (1.3.0) runs the same
compiled workflow with every side effect held and, where the template has one, over the
deployment's sample set -- the rehearse screen's numbers come from this, not from a
simulation of their own.

RunRequest.description: What to run over (1.6.0). Only a rehearsal reads it; a live run always polls the mailbox.

message_ids.description: With source mailbox, only these message ids; absent means every message matching the filter.

case_ids.description: With source cases or generated, only these cases; absent means every one.

RunTrigger.description: `regression` (1.6.0): a rehearsal over the golden cases the platform started because the use case changed.

ScheduleCadence.description:
The four the KPI shapes offer, plus the poll intervals a document-driven use case
offers (1.3.0): a mailbox is polled, not read nightly.

ScheduleDelivery.description: The delivery fields a framework `/schedules` row lacks. Everything else about a scheduled run -- cadence, pause, history -- is the framework's.

SkillRef.description: Which skill, at which version, produced something. Every prompt edit bumps the version, so a score drop is attributable (G13).

Snapshot.description: Which semantic version a read was answered from. On every response.

SourceTableStatus.description: One `source_tables` entry's own presentation detail -- its most recent load (from `quality.load_run`/`quality.load_stream_count`, the same rows the load pipeline itself writes) plus, when available, what the semantic layer and this KPI's own `table_usage` say about it.

loaded_at.description: When the load that produced this table's current row count finished. Null when the table has never loaded.

load_verdict.description: That load's own quality-gate verdict: `passed`, `blocked`, or `failed`.

description.description: The table's own description from the semantic layer (`Table.description`) -- what one row represents. Empty when the semantic layer has none, or is unreachable.

concepts.description: Ontology concepts this table is an instance of (`Table.concepts`, K8 mapping). Same visibility as `source_tables` itself -- concept names, not schema internals.

source_category.description: The table's coarse landing source (`crm`, `analytics`, `session_replay`) from the ingestion contract. Null for a table this deployment's landing contract does not name.

role.description: This KPI's own `table_usage` entry for the table, when it has one. Gated behind `kpis:write` the same way `sql` is -- null for a `kpis:read`-only caller regardless of whether the KPI has `table_usage` recorded.

join_note.description: This KPI's own `table_usage` join note for the table, when it has one. Same gate as `role`.

unused_columns.description: The table's columns, from the semantic layer, that this KPI's `column_usage` does not name. Gated behind `kpis:write` the same way `column_usage` is -- always `[]` for a `kpis:read`-only caller, and also `[]` when the KPI has no `column_usage` recorded (there is nothing to compute a remainder against) or the semantic layer is unreachable.

Spec.description:
What the author asked for, extracted by the spec-extraction agent (R9, Lane R's first
skill). Every closed-set value comes from the semantic layer and the vocabulary; an entity
the deployment does not have cannot appear here, it appears in `notes` instead.

notes.description: Empty on a clean extraction; otherwise what the question asked for that the deployment cannot express.

questions.description:
Clarifying questions for the author (1.1.0, R9). Where `notes` records what could not be
expressed, this records what the agent needs answered before the spec is complete -- a
metric it could not match to the registry, or a sentence ambiguous about whether the use
case should act. Empty on a clean extraction. A question is the refusal shape for an
unknown; the agent never coins a value to avoid asking one.

shape.description:
The shape the form was filled against (1.2.0, R-15). Null only on a spec extracted
before a shape was chosen; the compiler refuses a null shape rather than defaulting
to Inform.

template.description: The sequence within the shape, where the shape has more than one (1.2.0). Null means the shape's own sequence.

parameters.description:
The per-shape form's values, keyed by parameter name exactly as
`contracts.use_case.SHAPE_PARAMETERS[shape]` (or `TEMPLATE_PARAMETERS[template]`)
lists them (1.2.0, R-15): for Inform `metrics, dimensions, comparison, schedule,
recipient`; for Alert `metric, operator, threshold, scope, severity, recipient,
schedule`; for Recommend `candidates, metrics, guardrails, approver, write target,
timeout behaviour, schedule`; for Act `candidates, metrics, guardrails, write target,
per-run cap, rollback, schedule`; for the `document_to_record` template `source
mailbox, message filter, document type, extraction template, example document,
master data, match thresholds, guardrails, recipient, acknowledge, write target,
target objects, created as, per-run cap, rollback, schedule`. Keys may be written as
the name or its slug (`per-run cap` or `per_run_cap`). The gap check and the compiler
read this one place; a value the author typed on the form (the draft) still wins over
a value the extractor put here, and the compiled workflow records which.

Value shapes, so the interface and the compiler agree: `guardrails` is a list of
`{metric, operator (gte|lte), threshold, unit}` for the KPI shapes and a list of
`GuardrailRule` rows for `document_to_record` (1.4.0; the legacy `{id, param}` rows
naming the purchase-order preset -- duplicate_po, unknown_sender, first_time_product,
quantity_anomaly, due_date_sanity, restricted_product -- are still read);
`extraction template` is a shipped template's id or an `ExtractionTemplate` object
the form assembled (1.4.0); `target objects` is a shipped mapping's id or a
`RecordMapping` object the form assembled over the target's live fields (1.5.0); `candidates` is `{concept, filter}`;
`recipient` is `{who, channels[]}` where channels are `DeliveryChannel` values;
`master data` is `{customer, contact, shipTo, product, orderHistory}` naming
semantic-layer objects; `match thresholds` is `{address, product, name, ambiguity,
aiDisambiguation}`; `timeout behaviour` is one of `cancel, remind, escalate, proceed`;
`created as` is `draft` or `active`. Everything else is a string.

concept.description: A concept name from the semantic layer. Closed set, rendered from `GET /semantic/concepts`.

SuggestionContextSummary.description: What the agent read, for the review screen to show.

withheld_columns.description: Personal-data columns, as `table.column`, never shown to the agent.

concepts.description: Ontology concepts this table is an instance of, once mapping is confirmed (K8).

TableRef.description: A table's identity without its columns. What listing returns.

TableRole.description: How the formula uses one of its `source_tables` -- the same physical table can be the fact table for one KPI and a lookup for another, so this is per-KPI usage, not a property of the table itself.

TableUsage.description: How the formula uses one source table, paired with `ColumnUsage` to fill out "the data it reads".

join_note.description: One line naming what the join confirms or looks up, e.g. "Joined on linked_quote_id -> quote_id to confirm the quote exists". Empty for the fact table, which is read but not joined to anything.

TargetField.description: One createable field of a target object, read live (1.5.0).

type.description: The target's own type name: string, reference, date, double, picklist, ...

required.description: A create fails without it: not nillable and no default.

TargetObject.description: One object a write target lets the integration create (1.5.0), read live from the target.

TermOrigin.description: Whether the shipped ontology or the customer's overlay contributed a term (G10). Mirrors `egpt_retail.contracts.vocabulary.TermOrigin`.

kpi_identifier.description: The KPI a `kpi` tile reads. Null on a `query` tile.

grain_value.description: For a KPI at a non-overall grain, which row -- a supplier id, a location -- this tile shows. Null shows the top-N as a table.

description.description: Shown under the chart. Editable; never used to run anything.

rationale.description: Why the suggestion agent proposed this chart. Empty on a hand-built tile.

TileData.description: One tile's values from gold, with the stamp every gold row carries so a stale number is distinguishable from a wrong one.

delta.description: Change against the previous period at the same grain.

rows.description: For a `rowset` KPI, a table chart, or a `query` tile's cached result.

columns.description: Column order of `rows`, for a `query` tile. Empty on a `kpi` tile.

TilePatch.description: A partial edit of one tile. Every field optional; an omitted field is left unchanged. A changed `query` is re-checked by the guard and recomputed.

TileQuery.description:
A `query` tile's SQL and how its result maps onto the chart. `source_tables` is derived
by the server from the SQL at write time and returned for information; a client value is
ignored. Postgres dialect, one read statement, tables restricted to the semantic layer.

TileSource.description:
Where a tile's numbers come from. `kpi` (the default): a registered, ready KPI's gold
view. `query`: the tile's own SQL, checked by the warehouse read guard and cached on the
dashboard's refresh schedule.

TileWrite.description:
A tile to create or replace. `source` defaults to `kpi`, which requires `kpi_identifier`;
`query` requires `query`. `id`, when given on a whole-dashboard write, keeps that tile's
identity across the write instead of minting a new one -- what lets a per-tile edit leave
every other tile's id stable.

TimeWindow.description: A declared lookback relative to the run's as-of date. Never written into the SQL, so yesterday's number can be recomputed.

UseCase.description:
A use case is three artifacts -- a stored workflow component, the skill prompts its agent
steps carry, and a spec record holding what the author asked for. This is the catalog view
over all three. `level` is the autonomy level the activation screen shows; activating at
three or above needs the admin role (G11).

workflow_component_id.description: The framework component (`/components`) holding the compiled workflow, once one exists.

version.description: Bumped on publish. Runs and golden sets are attributed to a version (R15).

UseCaseDraft.description:
The builder's working state, steps one to nine. Persisted as a whole because the wizard
reads and writes it as a whole. Steps four and five (`plan_items`, `tasks`) are deliberately
absent: they are derived views served by `GET /use-cases/{id}/plan` over the compiled
workflow, never authored here -- a plan authored in parallel with the workflow is the
failure the build plan names.

UseCaseExecutionHealth.description: Execution health, from persisted run history. Free -- nothing here needs an assessment pass.

silent.description: The schedule should have fired and did not.

gates_waiting.description: Approval gates waiting on a person longer than their threshold.

status.description: The use case's own status (1.7.0), so a paused one is not reported silent.

schedule.description: The cadence it runs on (1.7.0), a `ScheduleCadence` value; null when it runs only on demand.

trigger.description: What fires the schedule where this platform runs (1.7.0): `poller` locally, `orchestrator` in the cloud, null when nothing does and the Run button is the only trigger.

next_expected_at.description: When the schedule should next fire (1.7.0), from the last run and the cadence.

exceptions_7d.description: Documents held with an exception across the last 7 days' live runs (1.7.0).

created_7d.description: Records created across the last 7 days' live runs (1.7.0).

error.description: Set instead of a real health snapshot when this one use case's own entry was malformed (e.g. a missing workflow_id) and its processing was isolated rather than aborting every other use case's report. Absent/null for a genuinely-run or genuinely-never-run use case.

UseCaseQuality.description: Is it still right -- the assessment pass over output quality and input drift (R14), separate from whether it ran. A use case that runs green while answering worse is what this catches.

golden_pass_rate.description: Share of the golden questions (R15) that passed on this version.

drift_score.description: Input distribution drift against the version's rehearsal baseline. 0 is none.

UseCaseRun.description: One run, keyed by use case and version (G12), holding its status, output reference and provenance reference. What "why did last Tuesday's run say that" hits.

framework_run_id.description: The framework's run id, for the session and run-history endpoints.

output_ref.description: Where the delivered answer lives -- a report id, or a knowledge document id once ingested (G12).

result.description:
What the run's last executor returned (1.3.0): for a document-to-record run, the batch
-- `documents` carried through with what was written, `exceptions` with their class and
detail, `stats` per stage, `rollback` -- so the interface shows what was created and what
was held without re-running anything. Null while queued or running, and for a run that
failed before any executor returned.

UseCaseShape.description:
What the use case does to the world (1.2.0, R-15): nothing, notify, write after a person
approves, write unattended. The shape is a property of the spec -- each shape has its own
form, chosen before the form is filled -- and it decides the parameter list, the workflow
the orchestration compiler generates, the readiness checks, and who may activate.
Mirrors `contracts.use_case.UseCaseShape`; the shipped vocabulary `use_case_shape` renders
the same four.

UseCaseSource.description: Whether the entry shipped with the product as a template or the customer authored it.

UseCaseSuggestion.description: A use case proposed from the connected data and the catalog (K13). Shares inputs and output discipline with KPI suggestion.

UseCaseTemplate.description:
The sequence within a shape, where a shape has more than one (1.2.0). `kpi_change` is the
Act sequence as section 07 describes it; `document_to_record` is the Act sequence a
document-driven automation needs -- receive, screen, extract, resolve -- before the same
guarded write. Both are Act. The interface reads the template from the requirement's own
words and never asks for it; the compiler checks it belongs to the shape.

template_id.description: When creating from a template, the template's id; the draft is prefilled from it.

post.summary: Accept many proposals in one decision. Not atomic -- see the response's `refused`.
post.description:
A harvest or a suggestion run produces many proposals at once; a gate per proposal is the
obvious tool and the wrong one (G5). **Deliberately not all-or-nothing**: an id that is
no longer pending (someone else decided it a moment earlier) is skipped and reported in
`refused`, and every other id in the request still commits -- eleven good decisions must
not be held hostage by a twelfth (K7's `ReviewOutcome`). Any `kind: kpi` ids that did
commit are adopted into the registry in the same call, same as the single-accept route.
Always `200`; check `refused` to see whether every id in the request actually moved.
